title.zh: 卷七十一 列傳第一: 后妃
title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第一: 后妃 Volume 71 Biographies 1: Emperesses and Consorts

sentences.zh: ○肅祖昭烈皇后蕭氏懿祖莊敬皇后蕭氏玄祖簡獻皇后蕭氏德祖宣簡皇后蕭氏太祖淳欽皇后述律氏太宗靖安皇后蕭氏世宗懷節皇后蕭氏世宗妃甄氏穆宗皇后蕭氏景宗睿知皇后蕭氏聖宗仁德皇后蕭氏聖宗欽哀皇后蕭氏興宗仁懿皇后蕭氏興宗貴妃蕭氏道宗宣懿皇后蕭氏道宗惠妃蕭氏天祚皇后蕭氏天祚德妃蕭氏天祚文妃蕭氏天祚元妃蕭氏

translations.literal: ○ Empress Zhaolie of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Su; Empress Zhuangjing of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Yi; Empress Jianxian of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Xuan; Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor De; Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan, consort of Taizu; Empress Jing'an of the Xiao clan, consort of Taizong; Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan, consort of Shizong; Consort Zhen of Shizong; Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Muzong; Empress Ruizhi of the Xiao clan, consort of Jingzong; Empress Rendé of the Xiao clan, consort of Shengzong; Empress Qin'ai of the Xiao clan, consort of Shengzong; Empress Renyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Xingzong; Imperial Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Xingzong; Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Daozong; Imperial Consort Hui of the Xiao clan, consort of Daozong; Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo; Virtuous Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo; Literary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo; Primary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo.
translations.idiomatic: ○ This chapter treats: Empress Zhaolie (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Su; Empress Zhuangjing (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Yi; Empress Jianxian (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Xuan; Empress Xuanjian (Xiao), wife of Ancestor De; Empress Chunqin (Shulü), wife of Taizu; Empress Jing'an (Xiao), wife of Taizong; Empress Huaijie (Xiao), wife of Shizong; Consort Zhen of Shizong; the Muzong empress (Xiao); Empress Ruizhi (Xiao), wife of Jingzong; Empress Rendé (Xiao), wife of Shengzong; Empress Qin'ai (Xiao), wife of Shengzong; Empress Renyi (Xiao), wife of Xingzong; Xingzong's imperial consort (Xiao); Empress Xuanyi (Xiao), wife of Daozong; Daozong's Consort Hui (Xiao); the Tianzuo empress (Xiao); Tianzuo's Virtuous Consort, Literary Consort, and Primary Consort (all Xiao).

sentences.zh: 《書》始嬪虞，《詩》興《關雎》。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents begins with the marriage at Yu; the Book of Songs opens with "Guan Ju."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents open with Shun's marriage alliance at Yu; the Odes begin with the "Ospreys," the classic prelude to wedded union.

sentences.zh: 國史記載，往往自家而國，以立天下之本。

translations.literal: National histories in their records often proceed from the household to the state, to establish the foundation of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic annals typically trace the realm from the imperial household outward, laying the foundation on which rule under Heaven rests.

sentences.zh: 然尊卑之分，不可易也。

translations.literal: Yet the distinction between superior and inferior cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the hierarchy of rank must never be confused.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷列呂后於《紀》；

translations.literal: Sima Qian placed Empress Lü in the "Basic Annals";
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian entered Empress Lü in the Basic Annals;

sentences.zh: 班固因之，而傳元后於外戚之後；

translations.literal: Ban Gu followed him, yet placed Empress Yuan in biography after the consort kin;
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu followed his lead but relegated Empress Yuan to a biography after the consort-kin section;

sentences.zh: 范曄登后妃於《帝紀》。

translations.literal: Fan Ye placed empresses and consorts in the "Imperial Annals."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye elevated empresses and consorts into the Imperial Annals.

sentences.zh: 天子紀年以敘事謂之《紀》，後曷為而紀之？

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's year-by-year narrative of events is called "Annals"—why should empresses be entered in Annals?
translations.idiomatic: Annals chronicle the ruler year by year—why place an empress among them?

sentences.zh: 自晉史列諸后以首《傳》，隋、唐以來，莫之能易也。

translations.literal: Since the Jin history placed all empresses at the head of "Biographies," from Sui and Tang onward none could change it.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin histories onward, empresses lead the biographical chapters—a convention unchanged since Sui and Tang.

sentences.zh: 遼因突厥，稱皇后曰「可敦」，國語謂之「脦俚寋」，尊稱曰「耨斡{麻女}」，蓋以配后土而母之雲。

translations.literal: The Liao followed the Turks in calling the empress "Kedun"; in the national language it was "Xielijian"; the honorific was "Nouwo Muanü"—meaning to pair with Queen Earth and mother the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Following Turkic usage, the Liao called the empress kedun; in Khitan it was xielijian, and the grand title nouwo muanü—pairing her with the earth goddess as mother of the people.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱帝，尊祖母曰太皇太后，母曰皇太后，嬪曰皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizu declared himself emperor, he honored his grandmother as Grand Empress Dowager, his mother as Empress Dowager, and his consort as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the imperial title, he styled his grandmother Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, and his principal consort Empress.

sentences.zh: 等以徽稱，加以美號，質於隋、唐，文於故俗。

translations.literal: Titles were matched in rank, fine epithets were added—substance drawn from Sui and Tang, ornament from ancient custom.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks were aligned with Chinese practice and graced with honorific epithets—substance from Sui and Tang, phrasing from older Khitan ways.

sentences.zh: 后族唯乙室、拔裏氏，而世任其國事。

translations.literal: The empress clans were only the Yishi and Bali, and generation after generation they held state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Yishi and Bali clans supplied empresses, and for generations they directed the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 太祖慕漢高皇帝，故耶律兼稱劉氏；

translations.literal: Taizu admired Han Emperor Gaozu, so the Yelü also took the surname Liu;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu revered Han Gaozu, and the Yelü house therefore also bore the surname Liu;

sentences.zh: 以乙室、拔裏比蕭相國，遂為蕭氏。

translations.literal: comparing the Yishi and Bali to Chancellor Xiao, they became the Xiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: likening the Yishi and Bali to Chancellor Xiao of Han, they adopted the surname Xiao.

sentences.zh: 耶律儼、陳大任《遼史·后妃傳》，大同小異，酌取其當，著於篇。

translations.literal: Yelü Yan and Chen Daren's "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts" in the Liao History differ in small ways; we have selected what is appropriate and set it down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The empress-and-consort biographies by Yelü Yan and Chen Daren in the earlier Liao History agree in the main but differ in detail; here we have chosen what fits and recorded it in full.

sentences.zh: 肅祖昭烈皇后蕭氏，小字卓真。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaolie of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Su, taboo name Zhuozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaolie (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Su, childhood name Zhuozhen.

sentences.zh: 歸肅祖，生四子，見《皇子表》。

translations.literal: She married Ancestor Su and bore four sons; see the Table of Imperial Sons.
translations.idiomatic: She wedded Ancestor Su and bore four sons, listed in the Table of Imperial Sons.

sentences.zh: 乾統三年，追尊昭烈皇后。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiantong, posthumously honored as Empress Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiantong 3 she was posthumously ennobled as Empress Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 懿祖莊敬皇后蕭氏，小字牙裏辛。

translations.literal: Empress Zhuangjing of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Yi, taboo name Yalixin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhuangjing (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Yi, childhood name Yalixin.

sentences.zh: 肅祖嘗過其家曰：「同姓可結交，異姓可結婚。」

translations.literal: Ancestor Su once passed her home and said, "Those of the same surname may form alliances; those of different surnames may marry."
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Su once passed her house and remarked, "Kin of the same surname may ally; those of different surnames may wed."

sentences.zh: 知為蕭氏，為懿祖聘焉。

translations.literal: Learning she was of the Xiao clan, he betrothed her to Ancestor Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning she was a Xiao, he arranged her betrothal to Ancestor Yi.

sentences.zh: 生男女七人。

translations.literal: She bore seven sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: She bore seven children in all.

sentences.zh: 乾統三年，追尊莊敬皇后。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiantong, posthumously honored as Empress Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiantong 3 she was posthumously ennobled as Empress Zhuangjing.

sentences.zh: 玄祖簡獻皇后蕭氏，小字月裏朵。

translations.literal: Empress Jianxian of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Xuan, taboo name Yueliduo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jianxian (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Xuan, childhood name Yueliduo.

sentences.zh: 玄祖為狠德所害，后嫠居，恐不免，命四子往依鄰家耶律臺押，乃獲安。

translations.literal: When Ancestor Xuan was killed by Hende, the empress lived as a widow and feared she would not escape harm; she sent her four sons to rely on their neighbor Yelü Taiya, and thus found safety.
translations.idiomatic: After Ancestor Xuan was murdered by Hende, the empress lived in widowhood and feared for her life; she sent her four sons to their neighbor Yelü Taiya, and only then were they safe.

sentences.zh: 太祖生，后以骨相異常，懼有陰圖害者，鞠之別帳。

translations.literal: When Taizu was born, the empress, seeing his bone structure was extraordinary, feared someone might plot against him in secret and raised him in a separate tent.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu's birth she saw his features were exceptional and, fearing secret plots against him, reared him in a separate camp.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，追尊簡獻皇后。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, posthumously honored as Empress Jianxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi 21 she was posthumously ennobled as Empress Jianxian.

sentences.zh: 德祖宣簡皇后蕭氏，小字巖母斤。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor De, taboo name Yanmujin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanjian (Xiao), wife of Ancestor De, childhood name Yanmujin.

sentences.zh: 遙輦氏宰相剔剌之女。

translations.literal: Daughter of the Yaonian chancellor Tila.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of Tila, chancellor of the Yaonian clan.

sentences.zh: 男、女六人，太祖長子也。

translations.literal: Six sons and daughters; she was mother of Taizu, the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: She bore six children; Taizu was her eldest son.

sentences.zh: 天顯八年崩，祔德陵。

translations.literal: She died in the eighth year of Tianxian and was buried at De Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Tianxian 8 and was interred at De Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，追尊宣簡皇后。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, posthumously honored as Empress Xuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi 21 she was posthumously ennobled as Empress Xuanjian.

sentences.zh: 太祖淳欽皇后述律氏，諱平，小字月理朵。

translations.literal: Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan, consort of Taizu, taboo name Ping, taboo childhood name Yueliduo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chunqin (Shulü), wife of Taizu, personal name Ping, childhood name Yueliduo.

sentences.zh: 其先回鶻人糯思，生魏寧舍利，魏寧生慎思梅裏，慎思生婆姑梅裏，婆姑娶勻德恝王女，生后於契丹右大部。

translations.literal: Her forebears were Uighur: Nuosi begot Wei Ning Shelila; Wei Ning begot Shensi Meli; Shensi begot Pogu Meli; Pogu married a daughter of King Yundeji and the empress was born in the Khitan Right Great Division.
translations.idiomatic: Her line traced to the Uighur Nuosi, then Wei Ning Shelila, Shensi Meli, and Pogu Meli; Pogu wed a daughter of King Yundeji, and the future empress was born in the Khitan Right Great Division.

sentences.zh: 婆姑名月碗，仕遙輦氏為阿紥割只。

translations.literal: Pogu's name was Yuewan; he served the Yaonian as Azha gazi.
translations.idiomatic: Pogu, called Yuewan, held the Yaonian office of azha gazi.

sentences.zh: 后簡重果斷，有雄略。

translations.literal: The empress was reserved, grave, decisive, and possessed heroic stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was austere and resolute, with a statesman's boldness.

sentences.zh: 嘗至遼、土二河之會，有女子乘青牛車，倉卒避路，忽不見。

translations.literal: Once when she came to the confluence of the Liao and Tu rivers, a woman in a green ox cart hastily left the road and suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the meeting of the Liao and Tu rivers she saw a woman in a green-ox cart who hurried from the path and vanished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，童謠曰：「青牛嫗，曾避路。」

translations.literal: Before long a children's song said, "The Green Ox Dame once yielded the road."
translations.idiomatic: Soon a children's rhyme ran, "The Green Ox Dame—she once gave way on the road."

sentences.zh: 蓋諺謂地祇為青牛嫗雲。

translations.literal: For the proverb calls the earth goddess the Green Ox Dame.
translations.idiomatic: The saying names the earth goddess the Green Ox Dame.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，群臣上尊號曰地皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, the ministers offered the honorific Earth Empress.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu's accession the court hailed her Earth Empress.

sentences.zh: 神冊元年，大冊，加號應天大明地皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shence, at the great investiture, the title Responsive-to-Heaven Great Illumined Earth Empress was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Shence 1, at the grand enthronement rites, she received the added title Responsive-to-Heaven, Greatly Illumined Earth Empress.

sentences.zh: 行兵禦眾，后嘗與謀。

translations.literal: In marching troops and commanding the masses, the empress often joined in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign and in commanding the host, she often shared in planning.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗渡磧擊党項，黃頭、臭泊二室韋乘虛襲之；

translations.literal: Taizu once crossed the desert to attack the Tangut; the Huangtou and Choubo divisions of Shiwei seized the opportunity to raid;
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu crossed the sands to strike the Tangut, the Huangtou and Choubo Shiwei bands struck at an opening;

sentences.zh: 后知，勒兵以待，奮擊，大破之，名震諸夷。

translations.literal: the empress learned of it, rallied troops to await them, struck fiercely, and routed them utterly—her fame shook all the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: she learned of it, mustered troops to meet them, attacked fiercely, and routed them; her name shook every tribe.

sentences.zh: 時晉王李存勖欲結援，以叔母事后。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jin Li Cunxu wished to form an alliance and addressed the empress as aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Li Cunxu then sought alliance and addressed her as aunt-by-marriage.

sentences.zh: 幽州劉守光遣韓延徽求援，不拜，太祖怒，留之，使牧馬。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang of Youzhou sent Han Yanhui to seek aid; he did not bow, and Taizu in anger detained him and set him to herd horses.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang of Youzhou sent Han Yanhui to plead for help; Yanhui would not bow, and Taizu in anger kept him and set him to tend horses.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「守節不屈，賢者也，宜禮用之。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "One who keeps his integrity and will not bow is a worthy man and should be received with rites and employed."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "A man who holds to his integrity and will not bow is worthy; receive him with ceremony and put him to use."

sentences.zh: 太祖乃召延徽與語，大悅，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Taizu then summoned Yanhui to converse with him, was greatly pleased, and made him his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then summoned Yanhui, took great delight in their talk, and made him chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 吳主李掞獻猛火油，以水沃之愈熾。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu, Li Yan, presented naphtha oil—which burns fiercer the more water is poured on it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu ruler Li Yan offered Greek fire; water only made it burn hotter.

sentences.zh: 太祖選三萬騎以攻幽州，后曰：「豈有試油而攻人國者？」

translations.literal: Taizu selected thirty thousand horsemen to attack Youzhou; the empress said, "How can one test oil and then attack another's state?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu chose thirty thousand horsemen to assault Youzhou; the empress said, "Who tests oil and then storms a whole kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 指帳前樹曰：「無皮可以生乎？」

translations.literal: She pointed to a tree before the tent and said, "Can it live without bark?"
translations.idiomatic: She pointed to a tree by the tent: "Can it live stripped of its bark?"

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「不可。」

translations.literal: Taizu said, "It cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu answered, "It cannot."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「幽州之有土有民，亦猶是耳。

translations.literal: The empress said, "Youzhou has land and people just the same.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Youzhou has soil and people—just the same.

sentences.zh: 吾以三千騎掠其四野，不過數年，困而歸我矣，何必為此？

translations.literal: If I raid their countryside with three thousand horsemen, within a few years they will be worn down and submit to us—why do this?
translations.idiomatic: Send three thousand riders to harry their fields; in a few years they will be spent and come to us—why take this risk?

sentences.zh: 萬一不勝，為中國笑，吾部落不亦解體乎！」

translations.literal: If we fail, China will laugh at us, and will not our tribes also fall apart!"
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, the Chinese states will mock us and our tribes may scatter!"

sentences.zh: 其平渤海，后與有謀。

translations.literal: In pacifying Bohai, the empress again shared in planning.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Bohai she again shared in the planning.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，后稱制，攝軍國事。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, the empress assumed regency and handled military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu's death she ruled in her own name and directed military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 及葬，欲以身殉，親戚百官力諫，因斷右腕納於柩。

translations.literal: At the burial she wished to follow him in death; kin and officials strongly remonstrated, so she cut off her right wrist and placed it in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral she meant to follow him in death; kin and officials pleaded until she severed her right wrist and laid it in the coffin.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded, she was styled Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 會同初，上尊號曰廣德至仁昭烈崇簡應天皇太后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, she was honored with the title Guangde Zhiren Zhaolie Chongjian Yingtian Imperial Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong she received the grand title Broad Virtue, Utmost Benevolence, Illustrious Martyr, Honored and Simple, Responsive-to-Heaven Imperial Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖嘗謂太宗必興我家，后欲令皇太子倍避之，太祖冊倍為東丹王。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu had said Taizong would surely revive our house; the empress wished the crown prince Bei to yield to him, and Taizu enfeoffed Bei as King of Eastern Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had once said Taizong would raise their line; the empress wanted Crown Prince Bei to step aside, and Taizu made Bei king of Eastern Dan.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，太宗立，東丹王避之唐。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, Taizong succeeded, and the King of Eastern Dan withdrew to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu's death Taizong took the throne, and the Eastern Dan king fled to Tang.

sentences.zh: 太后常屬意於少子李胡。

translations.literal: The empress dowager often set her hopes on the younger son Lihu.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager empress favored her younger son Lihu.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，世宗即位於鎮陽，太后怒，遣李胡以兵逆擊。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang; the empress dowager was angry and sent Lihu with troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died Shizong was enthroned at Zhenyang; the dowager, enraged, sent Lihu with an army against him.

sentences.zh: 李胡敗，太后親率師遇於潢河之橫渡。

translations.literal: Lihu was defeated; the empress dowager personally led troops and met the foe at Hengdu on the Huang River.
translations.idiomatic: Lihu was beaten; the dowager herself led forces and met the enemy at Hengdu ford on the Huang River.

sentences.zh: 賴耶律屋質諫，罷兵。

translations.literal: Thanks to Yelü Wuzhi's remonstrance, the armies were halted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yelü Wuzhi's counsel stopped the fighting.

sentences.zh: 遷太后於祖州。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was moved to Zuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager was relocated to Zuzhou.

sentences.zh: 應歷三年崩，年七十五，祔祖陵，謚曰貞烈。

translations.literal: She died in the third year of Yingli, aged seventy-five, and was buried at Zu Mausoleum with posthumous title Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Yingli 3, aged seventy-five, was buried at Zu Mausoleum, and received the posthumous name Steadfast Martyr.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，更今謚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, her present posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi 21 her current posthumous title was adopted.

sentences.zh: 世宗懷節皇后蕭氏，小字撒葛只，淳欽皇后弟阿古只之女。

translations.literal: Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan, consort of Shizong, taboo name Sagezhi, daughter of Empress Chunqin's younger brother Aguzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Huaijie (Xiao), wife of Shizong, childhood name Sagezhi, daughter of Aguzhi, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.

sentences.zh: 帝為永康王，納之，生景宗。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Yongkang, he took her in marriage and she bore Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: While he was Prince of Yongkang he wed her; she bore Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 天祿末，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianlu, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianlu she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，生萌古公主。

translations.literal: The next autumn she bore Princess Menggu.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn she bore Princess Menggu.

sentences.zh: 在蓐，察割作亂，弒太后及帝。

translations.literal: While she was in childbed, Chage rebelled and assassinated the empress dowager and the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Still in her lying-in, Chage rose in revolt and murdered the dowager and the emperor.

sentences.zh: 后乘步輦，直詣察割，請畢收殮。

translations.literal: The empress rode in a palanquin straight to Chage and asked that the burial rites be completed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress took a litter straight to Chage and begged leave to finish the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 明日遇害。

translations.literal: The next day she was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she too was slain.

sentences.zh: 謚曰孝烈皇后。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Empress Xiaolie.
translations.idiomatic: Her posthumous title was Filial and Martyr Empress.

sentences.zh: 重熙二十一年，更今謚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, her present posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi 21 her current posthumous title was adopted.

sentences.zh: 世宗妃甄氏，後唐宮人，有姿色。

translations.literal: Consort Zhen of Shizong, a palace woman of Later Tang, possessed beauty of form.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's consort Zhen, a Later Tang palace woman, was strikingly beautiful.

sentences.zh: 帝從太宗南征得之，寵遇甚厚，生寧王只沒。

translations.literal: The emperor obtained her on Taizong's southern campaign and favored her greatly; she bore Prince of Ning Zhimie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took her on Taizong's southern campaign and favored her deeply; she bore Prince of Ning Zhimie.

sentences.zh: 及即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 嚴明端重，風神閑雅。

translations.literal: Severe and bright, dignified and grave, her bearing was easy and refined.
translations.idiomatic: She was strict yet dignified, her manner calm and elegant.

sentences.zh: 內治有法，莫幹以私。

translations.literal: In inner governance she had method; none could sway her with private interest.
translations.idiomatic: She ran the inner court by rule, and no one could bend her with private pleas.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠、郭威稱帝，世宗承強盛之資，奄奄歲時。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan and Guo Wei declared themselves emperors; Shizong, inheriting a time of great strength, let the years slip idly by.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhiyuan and Guo Wei took imperial titles, Shizong, though he held a mighty inheritance, let year after year pass without action.

sentences.zh: 后與參帷幄，密贊大謀，不果用。

translations.literal: The empress joined in the command tent and secretly supported great plans, but they were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The empress joined council in the command tent and secretly urged bold plans, but none were adopted.

sentences.zh: 察割作亂，遇害。

translations.literal: When Chage rebelled, she met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Chage rebelled, she was killed.

sentences.zh: 景宗立，葬二后於醫巫閭山，建廟陵寢側。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he buried the two empresses at Mount Yiwulü and built temples beside the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong succeeded, he buried both empresses on Mount Yiwulü and raised shrines beside the royal tombs.

sentences.zh: 穆宗皇后蕭氏，父知璠，內供奉翰林承旨。

translations.literal: Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Muzong; her father Zhifan was Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance of the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong's empress (Xiao); her father Zhifan served as Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance of the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 后生，有雲氣馥郁久之。

translations.literal: At her birth, fragrant cloud vapor lingered long.
translations.idiomatic: At her birth fragrant clouds hung in the air for a long while.

sentences.zh: 幼有儀則。

translations.literal: In youth she had proper deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child she showed decorum.

sentences.zh: 帝居藩，納為妃。

translations.literal: While the emperor held a princely fief, he took her as consort.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still a prince he took her as consort.

sentences.zh: 及正位中宮，性柔婉，不能規正。

translations.literal: When she took the central palace, her nature was gentle and yielding; she could not correct him.
translations.idiomatic: Once she entered the central palace she was gentle and mild and could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: She had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: She bore no sons.

sentences.zh: 聖宗仁德皇后蕭氏，小字菩薩哥，睿知皇后弟隗因之女。

translations.literal: Empress Rendé of the Xiao clan, consort of Shengzong, taboo name Pusage, daughter of Ruizhi Empress's younger brother Weiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Rendé (Xiao), wife of Shengzong, childhood name Pusage, daughter of Weiyin, younger brother of Empress Ruizhi.

sentences.zh: 年十二，美而才，選入掖庭。

translations.literal: At age twelve, beautiful and talented, she was selected for the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve she was lovely and gifted and was chosen for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 統和十九年，冊為齊天皇后。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tonghe, she was enfeoffed as Empress Qitian.
translations.idiomatic: In Tonghe 19 she was enthroned as Empress Equal-to-Heaven.

sentences.zh: 嘗以草莛為殿式，密付有司，令造清風、天祥、八方三殿。

translations.literal: Once she made a straw model of a hall, secretly entrusted it to the officials, and ordered construction of the three halls Clear Wind, Heavenly Auspice, and Eight Directions.
translations.idiomatic: She once fashioned a straw model of a palace hall, handed it secretly to the works office, and ordered the building of Clear Wind, Heavenly Auspice, and Eight Directions halls.

sentences.zh: 既成，益寵異。

translations.literal: When they were completed, she was favored all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When they were finished, his favor for her deepened.

sentences.zh: 所乘車置龍首鴟尾，飾以黃金。

translations.literal: On the carriage she rode were placed dragon heads and owl-tail ornaments, adorned with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Her carriage bore dragon heads and owl-tail finials, all gilt in gold.

sentences.zh: 又造九龍輅、諸子車，以白金為浮圖，各有巧思。

translations.literal: She also made a Nine Dragons carriage and carriages for the princes, with pagodas of white gold—each showed ingenious design.
translations.idiomatic: She also commissioned a Nine Dragons imperial carriage and princes' coaches, setting white-gold pagodas on them—every piece bespoke clever invention.

sentences.zh: 夏秋從行山谷間，花木如繡，車服相錯，人望之以為神仙。

translations.literal: In summer and autumn when traveling through valleys, flowers and trees were like embroidery; carriages and robes intermingled—people gazing thought them immortals.
translations.idiomatic: In summer and autumn, as the court moved through mountain valleys where flowers bloomed like brocade and carriages and regalia flashed together, onlookers took them for immortals.

sentences.zh: 生皇子二，皆早卒。

translations.literal: She bore two imperial sons; both died young.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two imperial sons, but both died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 開泰五年，宮人耨斤生興宗，后養為子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaitai, the palace woman Noujin bore Xingzong; the empress raised him as her son.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaitai 5 the palace woman Noujin gave birth to Xingzong, whom the empress adopted as her own son.

sentences.zh: 帝大漸，耨斤詈后曰：「老物寵亦有既耶！」

translations.literal: When the emperor was gravely ill, Noujin reviled the empress: "Old creature—can favor last forever!"
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay dying, Noujin cursed the empress: "You old thing—does favor never end?"

sentences.zh: 左右扶后出。

translations.literal: Attendants helped the empress out.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants led the empress away.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，耨斤自立為皇太后，是為欽哀皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Noujin set herself up as empress dowager—this was Empress Qin'ai.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death Noujin made herself empress dowager—she who became Empress Qin'ai.

sentences.zh: 護衛馮家奴、喜孫等希旨，誣告北府宰相蕭浞卜、國舅蕭匹敵謀逆。

translations.literal: Guards Feng Jianu, Xisun and others to curry favor falsely accused Northern Chancellor Xiao Tubu and imperial uncle-in-law Xiao Pidi of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Guards Feng Jianu and Xisun, eager to please, falsely charged Northern Chancellor Xiao Tubu and the empress's uncle Xiao Pidi with treason.

sentences.zh: 詔令鞫治，連及后。

translations.literal: An edict ordered investigation, implicating the empress.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered an inquiry that implicated the empress as well.

sentences.zh: 興宗聞之曰：「皇后侍先帝四十年，撫育眇躬，當為太后；

translations.literal: Xingzong heard and said, "The empress served the late emperor forty years and nurtured my person—she should be empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong heard this and said, "The empress served my late father forty years and raised me—she ought to be empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 今不果，反罪之，可乎？」

translations.literal: now it fails—and instead she is charged with crime—is that right?"
translations.idiomatic: yet this is denied and she is punished instead—is that fitting?"

sentences.zh: 欽哀曰：「此人若在，恐為後患。」

translations.literal: Qin'ai said, "If this person remains, I fear future trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Qin'ai replied, "If she remains, she may become a future threat."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「皇后無子而老，雖在，無能為也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The empress is childless and old; though she remains, she can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "She is childless and old; even alive, she can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 欽哀不從，遷后於上京。

translations.literal: Qin'ai would not listen and moved the empress to Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin'ai refused and had the empress transferred to Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 車駕春蒐，欽哀慮帝懷鞠育恩，馳遣人加害。

translations.literal: During the emperor's spring hunt, Qin'ai feared he cherished the nurturing bond and hurriedly sent men to murder her.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's spring hunt, Qin'ai feared he still felt the debt of her upbringing and hurriedly sent assassins.

sentences.zh: 使至，后曰：「我實無辜，天下共知。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, the empress said, "I am truly innocent—all under Heaven know it.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came, the empress said, "I am truly innocent, as all the realm knows.

sentences.zh: 卿待我浴而後就死，可乎？」

translations.literal: Allow me to bathe before dying—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you let me bathe before I die?"

sentences.zh: 使者退。

translations.literal: The envoy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 比反，后已崩，年五十。

translations.literal: When he returned, the empress had already died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, the empress was already dead, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 是日，若有見后於木葉山陰者，乘青蓋車，衛從甚嚴。

translations.literal: That day some said they saw the empress on the shaded side of Mount Muye, riding a green-canopied carriage with a strict escort.
translations.idiomatic: That same day some claimed to see the empress on the north slope of Mount Muye, riding a green-canopied carriage with a stately guard.

sentences.zh: 追尊仁德皇后。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Empress Rendé.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously ennobled as Empress Rendé.

sentences.zh: 與欽哀並祔慶陵。

translations.literal: Buried jointly with Qin'ai at Qing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried with Qin'ai at Qing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 聖宗欽哀皇后蕭氏，小字耨斤，淳欽皇后弟阿古只五世孫。

translations.literal: Empress Qin'ai of the Xiao clan, consort of Shengzong, taboo name Noujin, fifth-generation descendant of Empress Chunqin's younger brother Aguzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qin'ai (Xiao), wife of Shengzong, childhood name Noujin, fifth-generation descendant of Aguzhi, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.

sentences.zh: 黝面狠視。

translations.literal: Dark of face, fierce of gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Her face was swarthy and her stare fierce.

sentences.zh: 母嘗夢金柱擎天，諸子欲上不能；

translations.literal: Her mother once dreamed of a golden pillar supporting Heaven; the sons wished to climb but could not;
translations.idiomatic: Her mother once dreamed of a golden pillar holding up the sky; her sons tried to climb it but could not;

sentences.zh: 後后至，與僕從皆升，異之。

translations.literal: when the future empress came, she and her servants all ascended—the mother marveled.
translations.idiomatic: when the future empress arrived, she and her attendants all climbed it—the mother was astonished.

sentences.zh: 久之，入宮。

translations.literal: After a time she entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In time she entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 嘗拂承天太后榻，獲金雞，吞之，膚色光澤勝常。

translations.literal: Once dusting Cheng Tian Empress Dowager's couch she found a golden cock, swallowed it, and her skin grew lustrous beyond the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Once while dusting Empress Dowager Chengtian's couch she found a golden rooster, swallowed it, and her complexion grew unusually radiant.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「是必有奇子！」

translations.literal: The dowager said, "She will surely bear an extraordinary son!"
translations.idiomatic: The dowager said, "She will surely bear an extraordinary son!"

sentences.zh: 已而生興宗。

translations.literal: Thereafter she bore Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after she bore Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 仁德皇后無子，取而養之如己出。

translations.literal: Empress Rendé had no son; she took him and reared him as her own.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Rendé, who had no son, took the boy and raised him as her own.

sentences.zh: 后以興宗侍仁德皇后謹，不悅。

translations.literal: The empress was displeased because Xingzong attended Empress Rendé with care.
translations.idiomatic: Noujin was displeased that Xingzong waited on Empress Rendé with filial care.

sentences.zh: 聖宗崩，令馮家奴等誣仁德皇后與蕭浞卜、蕭匹敵等謀亂，徙上京，害之。

translations.literal: When Shengzong died she had Feng Jianu and others accuse Empress Rendé, Xiao Tubu, Xiao Pidi and others of conspiracy, moved her to Shangjing, and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzong died she had Feng Jianu and others frame Empress Rendé and Xiao Tubu and Xiao Pidi for rebellion, exiled her to Shangjing, and had her killed.

sentences.zh: 自立為皇太后，攝政，以生辰為應聖節。

translations.literal: She set herself up as empress dowager and regent, making her birthday the Yingsheng Festival.
translations.idiomatic: She made herself empress dowager and regent and declared her birthday the Yingsheng Festival.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，尊為仁慈聖善欽孝廣德安靖貞純寬厚崇覺儀天皇太后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi she was honored as Benevolent, Sagely, Good, Filial, Broadly Virtuous, Peaceful, Tranquil, Chaste, Pure, Generous, Thick, Exalted, Awakened, Ceremonial, Heavenly Imperial Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi 1 she received the grand title Benevolent, Sagely, Good, Filial, Broadly Virtuous, Peaceful, Tranquil, Chaste, Pure, Generous, Honored, Awakened, Ceremonial, Heavenly Imperial Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 三年，后陰召諸弟議，欲立少子重元。

translations.literal: In the third year the dowager secretly summoned her younger brothers to discuss establishing her younger son Chongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the dowager secretly called her younger brothers to plot enthroning her younger son Chongyuan.

sentences.zh: 重元以所謀白帝，帝收太后符璽，遷於慶州七括宮。

translations.literal: Chongyuan revealed the plot to the emperor; the emperor seized the dowager's seals and moved her to Qikuo Palace at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyuan disclosed the plot to the emperor, who seized the dowager's seals and confined her at Qikuo Palace in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，帝悔之，親馭奉迎，侍養益孝謹。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year the emperor regretted it, personally drove to welcome her, and waited on her with growing filial care.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in year 6 the emperor repented, went in person to fetch her, and served her with ever stricter filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 后常不懌。

translations.literal: The dowager was often displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager remained often discontented.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，殊無戚容。

translations.literal: When the emperor died she showed no grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died she showed no sign of mourning.

sentences.zh: 見崇聖皇后悲泣如禮，謂曰：「汝年尚幼，何哀痛如是！」

translations.literal: Seeing Empress Chongsheng weeping properly, she said, "You are still young—why such mourning!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Empress Chongsheng weep in proper grief, she said, "You are still young—why such anguish!"

sentences.zh: 清寧初，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingning she was styled Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 崩，謚曰欽哀皇后。

translations.literal: She died; posthumous title Empress Qin'ai.
translations.idiomatic: She died and received the posthumous name Empress Qin'ai.

sentences.zh: 后初攝政，追封曾祖為蘭陵郡王，父為齊國王，諸弟皆王之，雖漢五侯無以過。

translations.literal: When she first held regency she posthumously enfeoffed her great-grandfather as Prince of Lanling, her father as King of Qi; all her younger brothers were made kings—even the Han Five Marquesses could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of her regency she posthumously made her great-grandfather Prince of Lanling and her father King of Qi; every younger brother became a king—a favor even the Han Five Marquesses never matched.

sentences.zh: 興宗貴妃蕭氏，小字三蒨，駙馬都尉匹裏之女。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Xingzong, taboo name Sanqian, daughter of Commander of the Horse Guards Pili.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong's imperial consort (Xiao), childhood name Sanqian, daughter of Commander of the Horse Guards Pili.

sentences.zh: 選入東宮。

translations.literal: Selected for the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She was chosen for the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，以罪降貴妃。

translations.literal: Early in Chongxi, for a crime she was demoted to imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongxi she was demoted to imperial consort for an offense.

sentences.zh: 道宗宣懿皇后蕭氏，小字觀音，欽哀皇后弟樞密使惠之女。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Daozong, taboo name Guanyin, daughter of Qin'ai Empress's younger brother, Commissioner of Military Affairs Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanyi (Xiao), wife of Daozong, childhood name Guanyin, daughter of Commissioner of Military Affairs Hui, younger brother of Empress Qin'ai.

sentences.zh: 姿容冠絕，工詩，善談論。

translations.literal: Her beauty surpassed all; she was skilled at poetry and good at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: None matched her beauty; she wrote poetry well and spoke with grace.

sentences.zh: 自制歌詞，尤善琵琶。

translations.literal: She composed lyrics herself and was especially skilled at the pipa.
translations.idiomatic: She wrote her own song texts and excelled above all on the pipa.

sentences.zh: 重熙中，帝王燕趙，納為妃。

translations.literal: Mid-Chongxi, when the emperor traveled in Zhao, he took her as consort.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongxi, while the emperor sojourned in Zhao, he took her as consort.

sentences.zh: 清寧初，立為懿德皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning she was established as Empress Yide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingning she was made Empress Yide.

sentences.zh: 皇太叔重元妻，以艷冶自矜，后見之，戒曰：「為貴家婦，何必如此！」

translations.literal: The wife of Imperial Uncle Chongyuan, proud of her seductive beauty—the empress saw her and warned: "As a great family's wife, why must you be thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Uncle Chongyuan's wife flaunted her allure; the empress saw her and admonished, "As a lady of a great house, why parade yourself so!"

sentences.zh: 后生太子浚，有專房寵。

translations.literal: Thereafter she bore Crown Prince Jun and held exclusive favor.
translations.idiomatic: Later she bore Crown Prince Jun and enjoyed his father's exclusive favor.

sentences.zh: 好音樂，伶官趙惟一得侍左右。

translations.literal: Fond of music, the entertainer Zhao Weiyi alone attended her at her side.
translations.idiomatic: She loved music, and the performer Zhao Weiyi alone waited on her.

sentences.zh: 大康初，宮婢單登、教坊朱頂鶴誣后與惟一私，樞密使耶律乙辛以聞。

translations.literal: Early in Dakang, palace maid Shan Deng and entertainer Zhu Dinghe falsely accused the empress and Weiyi of a private affair; Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelü Yixin reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dakang the palace maid Shan Deng and entertainer Zhu Dinghe accused the empress and Weiyi of adultery; Commissioner Yelü Yixin reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔乙辛與張孝傑劾狀，因而實之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yixin and Zhang Xiaojie to investigate and thereby substantiate it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict charged Yixin and Zhang Xiaojie to examine the case—and they made the charge stick.

sentences.zh: 族誅惟一，賜后自盡，歸其屍於家。

translations.literal: Weiyi's clan was executed; the empress was ordered to take her own life; her body was returned to her family.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyi's entire clan was executed; the empress was ordered to kill herself, and her body was sent home.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，追謚宣懿皇后，合葬慶陵。

translations.literal: Early in Qiantong, posthumous title Empress Xuanyi; buried jointly at Qing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiantong she was posthumously named Empress Xuanyi and buried with the emperor at Qing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 道宗惠妃蕭氏，小字坦思，駙馬都尉霞抹之妹。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Hui of the Xiao clan, consort of Daozong, taboo name Tansi, younger sister of Commander of the Horse Guards Xiamo.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong's Consort Hui (Xiao), childhood name Tansi, younger sister of Commander of the Horse Guards Xiamo.

sentences.zh: 大康二年，乙辛譽之，選入掖庭，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dakang, Yixin praised her; she was selected for the rear palace and established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Dakang 2 Yixin commended her; she entered the inner palace and was made empress.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，未見皇嗣。

translations.literal: Several years passed without an imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: After several years she had still borne no imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 后妹斡特懶先嫁乙辛子綏也，后以宜子言於帝，離婚，納宮中。

translations.literal: The empress's younger sister Wotelany had first married Yixin's son Suiye; the empress told the emperor on grounds of fitness for bearing children—they divorced and she was brought into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger sister Wotelany had wed Yixin's son Suiye; the empress told the emperor she would bear sons—they divorced, and Wotelany was brought into the palace.

sentences.zh: 八年，皇孫延禧封梁王，降為惠妃，徙乾陵；

translations.literal: In the eighth year imperial grandson Yanxi was enfeoffed Prince of Liang; she was demoted to Consort Hui and moved to Qian Mausoleum;
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 imperial grandson Yanxi was made Prince of Liang; she was demoted to Consort Hui and sent to Qian Mausoleum;

sentences.zh: 斡特懶還其家。

translations.literal: Wotelany was returned to her family.
translations.idiomatic: Wotelany was sent back to her family.

sentences.zh: 頃之，其母燕國夫人厭魅梁王，伏誅。

translations.literal: Soon her mother, Lady of Yan, used sorcery against the Prince of Liang and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon her mother, Lady of Yan, was found to have cursed the Prince of Liang and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 貶妃為庶人，幽於宜州，諸弟沒入興聖宮。

translations.literal: The consort was demoted to commoner and confined at Yizhou; her younger brothers were sent to Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was reduced to commoner rank and imprisoned at Yizhou; her brothers were sent to Xingsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 天慶六年，召還，封太皇太妃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianqing she was summoned back and enfeoffed Grand Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqing 6 she was recalled and titled Grand Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 後二年，奔黑頂山，卒，葬太子山。

translations.literal: Two years later she fled to Black Crest Mountain, died, and was buried at Prince Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later she fled to Black Crest Mountain, died there, and was buried at Prince Mountain.

sentences.zh: 天祚皇后蕭氏，小字奪裏懶，宰相繼先五世孫。

translations.literal: Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo, taboo name Duolilan, fifth-generation descendant of Chancellor Jixian.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo's empress (Xiao), childhood name Duolilan, fifth-generation descendant of Chancellor Jixian.

sentences.zh: 大安三年入宮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an she entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the palace in Da'an 3.

sentences.zh: 明年，封燕國王妃。

translations.literal: The next year she was enfeoffed Princess of Yan State.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she was made Princess of Yan.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: Early in Qiantong she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiantong she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 性閑淑，有儀則。

translations.literal: Gentle and modest in nature, with proper deportment.
translations.idiomatic: She was gentle and modest, with dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 兄弟奉先、保先等緣后寵柄任。

translations.literal: Brothers Fengxian, Baoxian and others through the empress's favor held power.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers Fengxian, Baoxian, and others rose to power through her favor.

sentences.zh: 女直亂，從天祚西狩，以疾崩。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen rebelled, she accompanied Tianzuo on the western hunt and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jurchen uprising she followed Tianzuo west on campaign and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 天祚文妃蕭氏，小字瑟瑟，國舅大父房之女。

translations.literal: Literary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo, taboo name Sese, daughter of the Great Father of the State Uncle's house.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo's Literary Consort (Xiao), childhood name Sese, daughter of the Great Father branch of the imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，帝幸耶律撻葛第，見而悅之，匿宮中數月。

translations.literal: Early in Qiantong the emperor visited Yelü Tage's residence, saw and delighted in her, and hid her in the palace for months.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiantong the emperor visited Yelü Tage's house, saw her and was smitten, and kept her hidden in the palace for months.

sentences.zh: 皇太叔和魯斡勸帝以禮選納，三年冬，立為文妃。

translations.literal: Imperial Uncle Heluwo urged the emperor to select and receive her by rites; in the winter of the third year she was established as Literary Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Uncle Heluwo urged the emperor to take her by proper ceremony; in the winter of year 3 she was made Literary Consort.

sentences.zh: 生蜀國公主、晉王敖盧斡，尤被寵幸。

translations.literal: She bore Princess of Shu and Prince of Jin Aolüwo and was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Princess of Shu and Prince of Jin Aolüwo and was especially cherished.

sentences.zh: 以柴冊，加號承翼。

translations.literal: By the charter ceremony the added title Bearer of Wings was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the investiture rite she received the added title Bearer of Wings.

sentences.zh: 善歌詩。

translations.literal: Skilled at songs and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in song and verse.

sentences.zh: 女直亂作，日見侵迫。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen trouble arose, daily more pressed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen rebellion broke out, the realm was pressed day by day.

sentences.zh: 帝畋遊不恤，忠臣多被疏斥。

translations.literal: The emperor hunted and feasted without concern; many loyal ministers were distanced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hunted and feasted without care while loyal ministers were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 妃作歌諷諫，其詞曰：「勿嗟塞上兮暗紅塵，勿傷多難兮畏夷人。

translations.literal: The consort composed songs of remonstrance; the words said: "Do not sigh on the frontier at dark red dust; do not grieve at many hardships and fear the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The consort composed remonstrance songs, which ran: "Do not sigh on the frontier at the dark red dust; do not shrink from hardship and fear the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 不如塞奸邪之路兮，選取賢臣。

translations.literal: Better block the path of treacherous ministers and select worthy servants.
translations.idiomatic: Better block the way of treacherous ministers and choose worthy servants.

sentences.zh: 直須臥薪嘗膽兮，激壯士之捐身。

translations.literal: You must sleep on brushwood and taste gall to stir warriors to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: You must sleep on brushwood and taste gall to stir brave men to give their lives.

sentences.zh: 可以朝清漠北兮，夕枕燕雲。」

translations.literal: Then at dawn you may clear the northern desert; at dusk pillow the Yan clouds."
translations.idiomatic: Then at dawn you may clear the northern desert, at dusk rest upon the Yan clouds."

sentences.zh: 又歌曰：「丞相來朝兮劍佩鳴，千官側目兮寂無聲。

translations.literal: She also sang: "The chancellor comes to court—sword and seals ring; a thousand officials look sidewise—in silence.
translations.idiomatic: She sang again: "The chancellor comes to court—sword and seals ring; a thousand officials glance aside—in utter silence.

sentences.zh: 養成外患兮嗟何及，禍盡忠臣兮罰不明。

translations.literal: Nurture outside calamity—alas too late; loyal ministers exhausted—punishment unclear.
translations.idiomatic: You have nurtured outside calamity—alas, too late; loyal ministers are spent—yet punishments are unclear.

sentences.zh: 親戚並居兮藩屏位，私門潛畜兮爪牙兵。

translations.literal: Kin all in border fief posts; private houses secretly train claw-and-fang troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kin fill every frontier post; private houses secretly raise armed retainers.

sentences.zh: 可憐往代兮秦天子，猶向宮中兮望太平！」

translations.literal: Pity the ages past—the Qin Son of Heaven, still from within the palace gazing at great peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Pity the Qin emperor of old—still from within the palace longing for peace!"

sentences.zh: 天祚見而銜之。

translations.literal: Tianzuo saw and resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo read them and bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 播遷以來，郡縣所失幾半，上頗有倦勤之意。

translations.literal: Since the flight, prefectures and counties lost were nearly half; the emperor showed weariness of office.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court's flight nearly half the commanderies and counties had been lost, and the emperor showed weariness of rule.

sentences.zh: 諸皇子敖盧斡最賢，素有人望。

translations.literal: Of all the imperial sons Aolüwo was most worthy and long had men's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Among the princes Aolüwo was the most worthy and had long enjoyed men's hopes.

sentences.zh: 元后兄蕭奉先深忌之，誣南軍都統余睹謀立晉王，以妃與聞，賜死。

translations.literal: Primary Consort's elder brother Xiao Fengxian deeply feared him; falsely accused Southern Army Commander Yudu of plotting to install the Prince of Jin, implicating the consort in knowledge—she was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Primary Consort's elder brother Xiao Fengxian deeply envied him; he falsely charged Southern Army Commander Yudu with plotting to enthrone the Prince of Jin and claimed the Literary Consort knew—she was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 論曰：遼以鞍馬為家，后妃往往長於射禦，軍旅田獵，未嘗不從。

translations.literal: Commentary says: The Liao took saddle and horse as home; empresses and consorts often excelled at archery and driving; on campaigns, hunts, and expeditions they seldom did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: The Liao made saddle and horse their home; empresses and consorts often excelled at archery and horsemanship, and on campaign, hunt, or march they seldom stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 如應天之奮擊室韋，承天之禦戎澶淵，仁懿之親破重元，古所未有，亦其俗也。

translations.literal: Such as Yingtian's fierce strike against Shiwei, Chengtian's bearing arms at Chanyuan, Renyi's personally breaking Chongyuan—unheard in antiquity, yet their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yingtian's fierce rout of the Shiwei, Chengtian's command at Chanyuan, Renyi's personal defeat of Chongyuan—such deeds are unheard in antiquity, yet they fit Khitan custom.

sentences.zh: 靖安無毀無譽；

translations.literal: Jing'an had neither praise nor blame;
translations.idiomatic: Jing'an won neither praise nor blame;

sentences.zh: 齊天巧思，乃奢侈之漸；

translations.literal: Qitian's ingenious designs were the beginning of extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Equal-to-Heaven's clever inventions marked the first drift toward extravagance;

sentences.zh: 宣懿度曲知音，豈致誣蔑之階乎？

translations.literal: Xuanyi set tunes and understood music—did that truly lead to the steps of false accusation?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanyi composed music and knew its tones—did that truly open the way to slander?

sentences.zh: 文妃能歌詩諷諫，而謂謀私其子，非矣。

translations.literal: The Literary Consort could sing and use poetry to remonstrate—yet to say she schemed for her son is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Consort sang and wrote verse to admonish the throne—yet to claim she plotted for her son is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 若簡憲之艱危保孤，懷節之從容就義，雖烈丈夫何以過之。

translations.literal: As for Jianxian's preserving the orphan in danger, Huaijie's calm acceptance of death—even fierce men could hardly surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxian's saving the orphan amid peril, Huaijie's calm facing of death—even resolute men could scarcely equal them.

sentences.zh: 欽哀狠桀，賊殺嫡後，而興宗不能防閑其母，惜哉！

translations.literal: Qin'ai was cruel and fierce, murdered the legitimate empress, yet Xingzong could not restrain his mother—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Qin'ai was ruthless and fierce, a murderer of the rightful empress, yet Xingzong could not restrain his mother—how regrettable!
